1 -- owned by the tickets the crosswalk's own `outside_the_population`
block names. A further 0 checks carry an edge without being declared by
any file, so they are counted in neither.

mean zero in the suite. As the declared population grows this projection
re-runs and fills.

none is written here. The [population_statement] guard refuses a
population figure that is not.

rows.claim: `Protocol.encode/1` of a Request yields a JSON object carrying `jsonrpc` `2.0`, the id, the method and the params
rows.evidence: protocol_test.exs:17-24 — `Request.new(1, "tools/list", %{"cursor" => "abc"})` encoded by `Protocol.encode(request)`, re-decoded, and then `assert decoded["jsonrpc"] == "2.0"`, `assert decoded["id"] == 1`, `assert decoded["method"] == "tools/list"` and `assert decoded["params"] == %{"cursor" => "abc"}`. The check's one axis is the filter `t.filter(e=>e.origin===` implementation — a spec-schema violation in a message OUR side sent is what fails it, since the emitting site reads `o.length===0` over exactly those violations — and the four asserts are the envelope the JSONRPCRequest schema requires of an outbound request. The DIRECTION is read off the bytes and not off the check's description: that filter, addressed at [325325,325367] in oc-axes-c1.json, is what scopes the check to messages the implementation sent.
